entries.reason: carried, and the getter is the header's own: ARPlaneAnchor.h:93 declares `@property (class, nonatomic, readonly, getter=isClassificationSupported) BOOL classificationSupported API_AVAILABLE(ios(12.0))`, so the selector is +isClassificationSupported and there is no +classificationSupported to look for. The ledger row's own reason ('neither -classificationSupported nor -setClassificationSupported: is an instance or a class selector') names the property, not the getter, and the release's class method list settles which one it is: ARPlaneAnchor's has two entries and one of them is +isClassificationSupported. The port answers NO (ARKit/ARAnchor.m), and NO is what the hardware gives: a plane's classification - floor, wall, table, ceiling, window, door - is read out of a depth sensor's geometry, and this device has neither TrueDepth nor LiDAR, which is the same reason the same file answers ARPlaneClassificationNone for -classification and ARPlaneClassificationStatusUnknown for -classificationStatus. Controls of the read: the class list resolves and prints its two entries with their implementation addresses, so a read that found nothing would print none
entries.effect: NO, which is what a device without a depth sensor answers; the call reaches a method the class itself carries, as it does on the release
